Class GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.robotics.navigation.GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive
public final class GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive extends Object
A RegulatedDifferentialDrive that holds its heading with a DirectionFinder, such as a GyroHeading. The wheels are regulated where the direction finder cannot reach them, on an RCX for instance, so the heading is corrected between moves: a straight travel is driven in segments, and after each segment the robot settles, the gyroscope measures how far its heading is from the one it should have, and a pivot about one wheel takes the error out.

By default a turn is left to the wheel encoders, and the heading the robot then has is the one later moves hold. A gyroscope read once a visit, between the infrared round trips that poll a moving pair, counts a fast rotation from a few reads, and a turn that ends between two of them loses what it turned meanwhile: on the reference build an encoder turn that looked exactly 90 degrees read 81, and correcting it made it worse. A straight segment rotates slowly, so its drift is measured well. With a buffered gyroscope, which loses no sample, setCorrectTurns(boolean) corrects turns to the heading asked as well.

A pivot's finest turn is one sensor step of one wheel, so an error below correctionDegrees is left: it must be at least half that step, or the pivot rounds to nothing (on 82 mm wheels and a 160 mm track with 16 steps a turn, a step is 5.8 degrees, so 3 degrees). Turns, headings and errors are all Cartesian degrees, counter-clockwise positive, as the drive's turns and the direction finder's directions are. Create it once at startup; its moves allocate nothing.

  • Constructor Details

    • GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive

      public GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive(RegulatedDifferentialDrive drive, DirectionFinder heading, int segmentMillimetres, int correctionDegrees, int settleMillis)
      Creates the drive. segmentMillimetres is the longest straight move between two heading checks, correctionDegrees the smallest error a pivot corrects, and settleMillis how long the robot is left to stop before the gyroscope is read.

  • Method Details

    • setCorrectTurns

      public void setCorrectTurns(boolean correctTurns)
      Whether a turn is corrected to the heading asked, as a straight segment is, rather than left to the encoders. Turn it on only with a direction finder that counts fast rotations whole, such as a GyroHeading over a BufferedGyroscope.

    • holdCurrentHeading

      public void holdCurrentHeading()
      Makes the current heading the one later moves hold, as if the robot had just been placed.

    • travelMillimetres

      public void travelMillimetres(int millimetres)
      Drives straight by millimetres, forward when positive, in segments of at most the configured length, and after each one corrects the heading back to the one held.

    • turnDegrees

      public void turnDegrees(int degrees)
      Turns in place by degrees, positive counter-clockwise, by the wheel encoders. With turns corrected, a pivot then takes out the error from the heading asked, which later moves hold. Otherwise the heading the robot has after the turn is held, and lastErrorDegrees() reports how far the direction finder saw the turn from the one asked, without acting on it.

    • corrections

      public int corrections()
      How many correcting pivots the drive has made.

    • lastErrorDegrees

      public int lastErrorDegrees()
      The heading error measured after the last move, before its correction, in degrees, counter-clockwise positive.

    • targetDegrees

      public int targetDegrees()
      The heading the drive holds, in degrees, counter-clockwise positive.
